name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+40 partisan lean makes a Democratic hold overwhelming
Chris Rabb has raised $1.3M with $1.6M in outside support, dwarfing the independent challenger
Prediction markets price the Democratic side at roughly 96%
Open seat after Dwight Evans's retirement, but no competitive opposition on the ballot
model.rationale: The D+40 fundamentals make this seat effectively unwinnable for the opposition, and Rabb's large financial edge plus markets pricing the Democratic side near 96% confirm it. No polls or expert ratings exist, but nothing in the evidence suggests meaningful risk.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or a late surge of outside spending against Rabb would be the only plausible route to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
This Philadelphia-area House seat is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+40. Dwight Evans is retiring, leaving an open seat, but the Democratic nominee Chris Rabb faces only an independent, Dennis Mahoney, who has raised about $10,800 with no outside support. Rabb has raised over $1.3 million and benefits from roughly $1.6 million in outside spending on his behalf.

Prediction markets put the Democratic side's chances near 96%, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no polls available, the forecast rests on the district's overwhelming fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold in the low-to-mid 30s in margin.
